Two murals celebrating a former railway line have been approved for a disused bridge between Brampton and Grafham. Huntingdonshire District Council has granted advertisement consent for the artwork on the underside of the railway bridge on Grafham Road, Brampton. The decision was issued today (Friday). The two murals will each measure approximately 2.5 metres high by four metres wide and will be painted directly onto the underside of the bridge. Historic railway bridge murals celebrating area's past given the green light. (Image: HDC) The designs will feature predominantly cream text against a dark blue background, with the colours chosen to reflect the historic railway livery associated with the former line. The bridge is on a designated Quiet Road between Brampton and Grafham, surrounded by agricultural fields to the south and Brampton Wood to the north. Planning officers said the artwork had been designed to reflect the historic significance of the former railway and would provide a “cultural and heritage reference” sympathetic to the character of the area.
